engagement_title: Halden Greens first paid push: build one creator led ad and its platform set from five phone clips, and carry the hooks onto editable caption cards and a matched thumbnail without making any of it look expensive
vertical: Health and wellness, direct to consumer daily greens subscription, online only with a creator seeded audience (Portland, Oregon)
real_brief_anchor: GROUNDED in the real PeoplePerHour brief 'Video Ads for DTC Supplement Brand (UGC / VSL / Mashup)', quoted in the ledger grounding_note: a direct to consumer supplement brand supplies a batch of raw user generated talking head creator clips plus product b roll and wants them cut into short paid social ad variants testing DIFFERENT HOOKS, each reframed to the platform native ratios, with on brand text, captions and callout graphics added, and platform ready cuts plus a scroll stopping thumbnail delivered, conversion focused and fast. The posted brief names no client, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional brand Halden Greens. The real post treats the caption and hook layer as an afterthought bolted onto the cut; CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what lets this be built as the client actually needs it, because HTML authoring returns a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes, which turns 'we will be swapping hooks every week' from a promise into a deliverable the growth lead can operate without recommissioning anyone.
client_one_liner: We sent tubs to three creators, we have five clips filmed on their own phones and some counter footage our founder shot, and we are about to put real money behind one ad that has to look like something a friend sent you.
client_brief:
Halden Greens, first paid push

We sell a daily greens powder on subscription, fifty nine dollars a month, mostly to people between twenty five and forty who have already been burned by a supplement that promised too much. They do not trust anything that looks like an advert. That is the whole problem we are hiring you to solve.

What we have. Five clips from three creators we sent tubs to, filmed on their own phones in their own kitchens. They are not polished and we do not want them polished. Alongside them, four short clips of the tub, the scoop and the pour that our founder shot on the counter at home, and a handful of photographs the creators sent us. One creator clip is our favourite by a distance: she is funny, and she says the thing about the morning routine that everyone repeats back to us.

What we need. One short ad cut from that material that feels like something a friend sent you rather than something an agency made. It has to run in the vertical feeds, in the square feed and in the four by five slot, and we are spending real money behind it, so those versions have to be right rather than squeezed. Tell us which clip you built the cut around and why.

Captions matter more than anything here. Our growth lead wrote six hook lines. We want them as cards we can change ourselves week to week, because we will be testing and swapping them constantly and the wrong hook is the difference between this working and not. They sit over the footage, so they have to stay readable over a bright kitchen and over a dark counter. Tell us plainly which hooks you would not run, and why.

We also need one still for the thumbnail slot, matched to the ad. Our platform asks for 1280 by 720 there. And the tub cut out cleanly, because it sits on our green panel.

Our logo only exists as a flat export. Nothing here should look expensive.
price_band_and_audience: Fifty nine dollars a month on subscription, buyer 25 to 40, health literate and specifically sceptical of polish. The band is load bearing in an unusual direction: the money is real but the look must be cheap, because at subscription economics the acquisition cost is decided by whether the ad survives being recognised as an ad. Grade lightly, keep the phone framing, keep the room noise short of unintelligible, set the hooks in plain type at conversational length. The same product at a hundred and forty dollars a month would correctly be shot in a studio, graded cool and clean, with restrained type and generous space, and shipping that treatment here reads as a company pretending to be a person, which is the single most expensive mistake available on this brief. Push the other way into flashing text, countdowns and stacked badges and it reads as a fifteen dollar tub, which contradicts the subscription price. A posted job of this shape runs 700 to 1,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Direct to consumer daily greens powder sold online on a monthly subscription, creator seeded.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2023, Portland, Oregon, online only, a small founder led team with a growth lead and three seeded creators.
brand_identity.about: Halden Greens is a daily greens powder people actually keep drinking, sold by subscription to buyers who have already been let down by a supplement that promised too much. We grow by putting the product in real kitchens and letting real people talk, not by looking like an advert. That distrust of polish is the brand.
brand_identity.audience: Health literate adults 25 to 40 who are specifically wary of supplement marketing and trust a friend's recommendation over a glossy campaign.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Fifty nine dollars a month on subscription. Priced as a considered daily habit, above the fifteen dollar tub and below the studio shot premium brands. The money is real, so the look must never be.
brand_identity.typography: One friendly, near neutral sans set at conversational size, plain weights only. Type should look unconsidered while being entirely considered: no countdowns, no stacked badges, no burst text. Hooks read like a caption a person typed, not a headline.
brand_identity.voice: Conversational, honest to a fault, a little self aware, never hype. Example: "We are not going to tell you it changed our life. It is greens. You drink them in the morning."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark exists only as a flat export, dark disjoint letters on white, with no vector source. The brand green panel is fixed and every cutout has to hold against it. Some earlier photography still shows a previous tub label and should not be reused.
brand_identity.values: Say only what we can stand behind. Claims live inside the category compliance sheet, and anything the sheet forbids does not run, however good the line.

assets_supplied.name: halden_creator_clips/ (5 clips, 3 creators)
assets_supplied.kind: Talking head clips filmed by creators on their own phones in their own kitchens, tub in hand, no scripts, no lighting.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Five clips, three creators. The second one from Mara is the one we love."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the five are horizontal with the creator hard left of frame, so a square reframe puts the tub outside the picture entirely, and the favourite clip is one of those two. One clip's audio sits at roughly half the level of the others and carries street noise through an open window, so a single levelling decision applied to the set leaves either that creator inaudible or the rest harsh.

assets_supplied.name: halden_founder_broll/ (4 counter clips)
assets_supplied.kind: Short handheld clips of the tub, the scoop and the pour, shot by the founder on the kitchen counter at home.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The product shots, filmed at my place. Use whichever help."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the four are the same pour from the same angle seconds apart, so a cut that uses both reads as a stutter, and one was captured at a different frame rate from the rest, which no filename shows and which cannot be reconciled here.

assets_supplied.name: halden_creator_stills/ (6 phone photographs, 4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: Photographs the creators sent alongside the clips: tub on a counter, tub in hand, a mug beside it.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Whatever they sent us. Better quality than the video, I think."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The only frame where the tub is held clearly is backlit by the window behind the counter, so the pale mint lid runs at almost the same value as the sunlit worktop and a one call knockout bites the lid edge while returning a complete looking cutout. Two of the six show the previous tub design with the older label.

assets_supplied.name: halden_thumb_hero.jpg (1080 x 1920)
assets_supplied.kind: A still the growth lead pulled out of the favourite clip and sent over as the intended thumbnail.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This frame. This is the expression we want on the thumbnail."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a screen grab from a vertical clip rather than a camera file, so the platform's 1280 by 720 slot cannot be reached from it without enlargement, which the crop tool will perform up to a two times cap while reporting it only inside its own tradeoff record. Cropping it to a wide ratio also clips the tub out of the frame.

assets_supplied.name: halden_wordmark.png
assets_supplied.kind: Flat export of the wordmark, dark disjoint letterforms on a white ground, no vector file.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Disjoint lettering collapses under a one call knockout, which returns two surviving letterforms at full success, and a trace returns geometry with no viewBox and an opaque full canvas ground path riding underneath it.

assets_supplied.name: halden_hooks.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Six hook lines written by the growth lead, plus the brand's own one page compliance sheet listing what the category cannot claim.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Six hooks. We think three of them are the strong ones."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the six make a comparative health claim the brand's own compliance sheet forbids, and nothing marks which. A third runs to fourteen words, which cannot hold at vertical caption size without dropping to a point size at which it stops functioning as a hook.

assets_supplied.name: halden_tone_reference.png
assets_supplied.kind: A screenshot the founder saved of an ad in an unrelated category whose register she likes, supplied as a tone reference only.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is the feeling. Not the look, the feeling."

acceptance_bar: The cut reads as creator footage rather than as an agency edit: phone framing kept, grading restrained, room sound present but the speech intelligible throughout. A polished version fails this brief even if it is technically cleaner.
Every platform version keeps the product in frame for the whole time it is on screen. A reframe that centres the picture and loses the tub fails.

No delivered file, still or motion, exceeds the pixel dimensions of the source it derives from, and no returned resize record carries an enlargement entry. A thumbnail brought to size by enlargement fails even if it looks acceptable.

Where a slot cannot be reached at the platform's stated size from source scale, it is named with the reason and with the size actually delivered. Silently delivering short fails, and so does enlarging to hit the number.
Audio is levelled per clip rather than by one setting across the set, and the quietest creator is audible without the others becoming harsh.

Every hook that reaches a card is one the brand's own compliance sheet permits, and the ones that do not are named in the note with the reason. A compliant looking card carrying a forbidden claim fails.
Each hook card is readable over the footage it plays on, over the bright kitchen and over the dark counter, at the size it actually appears. A caption that is legible only at full canvas fails.

The hook cards arrive as ONE working file carrying all three canvas sizes, each keeping its own size, with live retypeable text so the growth lead can swap a hook without a designer, and the mark as real vector shapes.
The caption text is actually present and actually visible on all three canvases, not only on the first one.
The tub cutout holds its edge when placed on the brand's green panel, not only when viewed against white.

The note states which clip the cut was built around and why, which hooks were rejected and on what grounds, what the footage could not give, every resize any tool reported, and which stills show the previous tub.

adobe_surfaces.role: The ad itself. It establishes what each of the nine supplied files actually is rather than what the folder implies, locates where each hook line lands inside the talking head material, shortens the chosen material into a mashup whose length suits a sceptical scroller, levels and cleans the creator audio clip by clip rather than by one setting, and produces the three platform slots inside source scale with the product held in frame.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_fill_area, image_remove_background, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: The still half. It brings the usable creator photographs to one restrained target that does not out polish the footage, isolates the tub for the overlay cards and for the brand panel, builds the thumbnail honestly at source scale while reading what every crop reports about its own dimensions, and recovers the wordmark off a flat disjoint export with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for you.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The hook cards as one native editable document carrying three canvas sizes, which is the only way the growth lead can swap a hook weekly without recommissioning anyone. Photography has to be carried as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, the mark goes in as inline SVG so it stays vector, family and weight are declared per text element, and the payload travels by uploaded URL because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type for the hook cards and the thumbnail, where the art direction problem is unusual: the type has to look unconsidered while being entirely considered. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame nobody shot, a clean counter ground at genuine camera scale for the end card, IP clean and with generative candidates excluded, on a brief where anything that reads as bought is actively harmful. The Boards half persists the hook shortlist the growth lead signs off from, placed within the twelve per call cap, with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unacceptable there.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The cut and the slots are motion work; the hook cards must be an authored editable document because they are swapped weekly; the thumbnail and the cutout are raster work with a hard spec. The brief pins all three, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role, because nine video files and six photographs from three creators are otherwise indistinguishable by filename.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Read what each of the nine supplied video files actually is: orientation, dimensions, duration and frame rate, and where the creator sits in frame.
trajectory.judgement: The client's favourite clip and the clip that can carry a square slot are not necessarily the same clip, and that can only be settled from what the files are. Establishing it before cutting is the difference between a delivery plan and a promise the footage cannot keep.
trajectory.produces: A per file record of orientation, scale, duration and subject position.

trajectory.action: Summarise the creator clips to locate where each hook line, and the morning routine line the client values, actually falls inside them.
trajectory.judgement: A hook card that names a claim the cut never makes is worse than no card. The material decides which hooks are even available.
trajectory.produces: A map of which spoken material sits in which clip and roughly where.

trajectory.action: Level and clean the creator audio one clip at a time, judging the quiet street noise clip against the others rather than applying one setting to the set.
trajectory.judgement: One setting across five phone recordings made in five rooms either buries one creator or makes the rest harsh. The floor here is intelligibility, not silence, because room sound is part of what makes this read as a person.
trajectory.produces: Per clip cleaned audio with the parameters applied recorded per clip.

trajectory.action: Cut the mashup around the chosen creator material, at a length that suits a sceptical scroller rather than a brand film.
trajectory.judgement: The cutting tool shortens and chooses its own moments, so the agent's control is what it is handed and how long the result is asked to be. Choosing the clip to build around is the single biggest craft decision in the engagement and the client has asked to be told which one it was.
trajectory.produces: One short creator led cut, with the choice of anchor clip written down.

trajectory.action: Produce the three platform slots inside source scale, deciding per clip rather than per set, and name any slot that cannot be reached at the platform's stated size.
trajectory.judgement: Reframing is downscale only, and a horizontal clip with the creator hard left does not survive a centred square crop. Where the favourite material cannot serve a slot, the honest answer is a different anchor for that slot or a named shortfall, not an enlargement.
trajectory.produces: The platform set with the product held in frame throughout, plus a written statement of what could not be reached.

trajectory.action: Look at the six creator photographs and triage them: which show the current tub, which show the previous label, how each is lit, and where the tub separates from its ground and where it does not.
trajectory.judgement: The client believes the photographs are better quality than the video, which is true of their pixel count and not of their usability. Which frames show the current packaging is a question only the pictures can answer.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering tub design, lighting and subject separation.

trajectory.action: Bring the usable stills to one restrained target that sits beside the footage rather than above it, recording every parameter applied.
trajectory.judgement: The temptation here is to make the stills good. The correct target is stills that look like they came off the same phone as the cut, which is a harder and less satisfying thing to aim at.
trajectory.produces: A graded still set at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Isolate the tub for the overlay cards and for the brand panel, and inspect the cut edge on the green panel rather than against white.
trajectory.judgement: A cutout is judged on the ground it will actually sit on. Backlit packaging against a sunlit worktop is exactly where a knockout has least to work with, and white hides precisely the failure the green panel exposes.
trajectory.produces: A tub cutout with genuine alpha, inspected on the destination ground.

trajectory.action: Build the thumbnail at source scale, reading every returned resize record, and name the slot size that cannot be reached honestly from the frame the client chose.
trajectory.judgement: The client picked the frame for the expression, which is a legitimate reason, and it does not make the arithmetic work. The choice is between a different source frame, a smaller honest delivery, or an enlargement that fails the bar, and the client has to be told which was taken.
trajectory.produces: A thumbnail candidate at source scale with its resize record transcribed and the shortfall, if any, stated.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the counter ground the end card needs, filter to photography, exclude generative candidates, license and download at full resolution, then set it beside the graded creator material.
trajectory.judgement: On this brief the risk is not licensing quality, it is that quality itself is the tell. The frame has to survive sitting next to phone footage.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame, judged in the company of the set it has to join.

trajectory.action: Recover the wordmark: an ink level selection naming the letterforms' own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own bbox, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the ink rather than the sheet, which polarity to trace, and the fact that a knockout is the wrong instrument entirely on disjoint lettering.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and the brief inverts the usual target: the type has to look unconsidered. Weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Read the six hooks against the brand's own compliance sheet and against the measure each canvas actually gives, and decide which hook runs where.
trajectory.judgement: Two things disqualify a hook here and only one of them is visible in the writing. A fourteen word line is not saved by setting it smaller, because a hook that has to be read carefully is not a hook.
trajectory.produces: A hook to canvas assignment plus a written list of what was rejected and on what grounds.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying three roots at three canvas sizes, inline the photography as image data, place the mark as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, declare family and weight on every text element, upload the file, run the readiness check and export.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is making a caption that holds over both a bright kitchen and a dark counter without looking designed.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML and a native editable Express document, with the HTML retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Verify the exported document through both channels that exist: resolve its rendition and look at the first canvas, then parse the returned per canvas markup for the other two.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at card one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: An inspected first canvas and a per canvas markup audit for the other two.

trajectory.action: Create the hook shortlist board, add the card renders, the thumbnail candidates and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is not a success, and the vector mark is not boardable so it belongs in the note instead. The note has to answer the two questions the client actually asked: which clip, and which hooks would you not run.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover mapping hooks to formats.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the tub actually separates from its ground on the one photograph where it is held clearly. That frame is backlit by the window behind the counter, so the pale mint lid runs at very nearly the value of the sunlit worktop, and the knockout returns a cutout that is clean, complete and entirely convincing at preview scale while having bitten the lid edge where the two values meet. Nothing in the response indicates it, the alpha reads as a normal feathered edge, and against white the bite is invisible because what was removed was white. It appears only once the cutout is placed on the brand's green panel at the size it actually runs.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because where a subject and its ground share value is a property of this specific photograph and is not legible by looking at the frame beforehand. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the tub sits on the green panel, which is a placement requirement, and the acceptance line about the edge holding on the panel is the client's own standard rather than a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different chain, a positive selection of the packaging by its own material properties, inverted and filled, rather than the same knockout again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re cut the tub through an explicit selection route, or move to a different source photograph and re grade it into the set, then inspect every candidate on the green panel at running size before any card is authored around it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An ad set whose product, the only object the entire campaign is selling, sits on the brand panel with a chewed lid edge at the exact moment the viewer looks at it, on a brief whose whole premise is that the audience is already sceptical.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the construct the hook captions depend on. Caption text that has to survive both a bright kitchen and a dark counter is naturally set with an outline around the letterforms, and that outline is discarded, with the letterforms themselves rendered as fully transparent when the outline was carrying the colour, so the caption is present in the document and invisible on the canvas. The soft drop behind text, the other standard legibility route, is discarded as well. All of it returns success with no warning, the returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's rendition returns the first artboard only, so the second and third cards can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and getting it right first time presumes knowing which of several equally standard legibility constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for captions that stay readable over bright and dark footage, which is the requirement the construction was chosen to satisfy. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different construction entirely, legibility carried by a solid or gradient plate behind the words or by an upstream raster treatment, and the caption re composed around whichever it is.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re author the cards on a surviving legibility route, possibly producing a differently treated raster upstream for the type to sit on, upload again, run the readiness check again, export again, and audit all three canvases from the returned markup rather than from the first card.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A hook card file handed to a growth lead who swaps hooks weekly in which the hooks themselves are invisible on two of the three canvases, spending real media money behind an ad whose single most important element is not there.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the licensed frame can sit in this company at all. The choice is made from a thumbnail rendition a couple of hundred pixels across, at which warmth, grain and styling all read as domestic. The full resolution file is the first place the frame's true colour, its lighting and its production values exist, and a counter shot that looked like somebody's kitchen at thumbnail size can resolve as evenly lit, propped and commercially styled once it is downloaded and set beside phone footage. On any other brief that would be an upgrade. Here it is the defect, and it cannot be seen until the two are adjacent.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the only preview available before licensing is the small rendition and the comparison that matters requires the graded set to already exist. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says nothing should look expensive, which is the direction, not a disclosure that a specific licensed frame will violate it. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different decision, licensing a different candidate or abandoning the licensed route entirely and building the end card on a flat house panel with a creator still.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re run the search with a different query, license and download an alternative and judge it beside the graded set again, or drop the stock route and rebuild the end card from material that was actually shot on a phone, then re author whatever the card was carrying.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An ad that holds its creator register for its whole length and then ends on a frame that is visibly a stock photograph, which is precisely the moment a sceptical viewer decides the preceding thirty seconds were an advert after all.

deliverables.name: Halden creator ad and platform set

Every slot either delivered at the platform's stated size or reported as unreachable with the reason and the size actually delivered.

deliverables.name: Halden hook cards, three canvases, as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document carrying three roots at three canvas sizes, each hook set as live retypeable text so the growth lead can swap it without a designer, the mark as real vector shapes, and every caption actually visible and readable over the footage it plays on, on all three canvases. Only compliance permitted hooks reach a card. Delivered with the self contained source HTML, which is the durable half, since the hooks change weekly.

deliverables.name: Halden thumbnail and matched still set

Per frame parameter log.

deliverables.spec: The tub isolated with genuine alpha and an edge that holds on the brand's green panel at running size rather than only against white, paired with the wordmark recovered from a flat disjoint export as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground, a real viewBox present and no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it.

verifiers_auto.how: Diff the returned tradeoff objects from every image and video call against the resize and shortfall table in the note.

verifiers_auto.text: Three platform versions exist at three distinct aspect ratios, each derived from a source at or above its delivered scale.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the dimensions of each delivered version and trace each to its stated source in the manifest.

verifiers_auto.text: The tub cutout carries genuine alpha rather than a filled rectangle, with full transparency at the frame corners and partial alpha at the packaging boundary.
verifiers_auto.how: Inspect the alpha channel of the delivered cutout at the corners and along the lid edge.

verifiers_auto.text: The Express export returned three canvases, each keeping its own declared size.
verifiers_auto.how: Read slide_count and the per canvas width and height in the export response.

verifiers_auto.text: Every hook card's caption text is present in the returned markup with a visible colour value, and no text node resolved to a fully transparent fill.

How long the cut should run for a buyer whose first instinct is to scroll past anything that looks bought.

Which creator photographs show the current packaging, and how to say so when two of them do not.

Which of the six hooks the brand's own compliance sheet actually permits, and which are simply too long to function at vertical size.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a polished supplement ad, which is precisely the artefact this client is paying not to receive. IDENTITY: these are three real creators saying specific things about a specific tub with a specific current label, and the value of the ad is that those people said those words. A regenerated spokesperson is fraud and a regenerated tub is the wrong packaging. SPEC: the platform slots have stated sizes that must be met from source scale with nothing enlarged, the thumbnail slot is an exact size the chosen frame cannot honestly reach, and the cutout has to carry real alpha onto a brand panel, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the hook cards exist to be swapped weekly by the growth lead, so a picture of a caption is worthless, and the compliance filter is a judgement about claims rather than a rendering problem. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did this knockout bite the lid, did this caption survive the import, does this licensed frame still read as a kitchen when it is full size.
doability_proof: Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING is fully headless across 27 live calls: apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and upscale_factor, fill_area, remove_background in both forms, and vectorize. The three checkpoints rest on documented live findings rather than assumptions: remove_background is confirmed to fail where a subject offers no contrast against its ground while reporting success loudly, and alpha is verified to survive crops at outputFileType png (13,371 partial alpha pixels preserved), so the green panel test is real; the importer DROPS webkit text stroke and, combined with a transparent fill, writes the text as fully transparent, and text shadow is dropped as well, both at HTTP success, with the rendition documented as PAGE 1 ONLY; and Stock renditionURL is documented as a 240 px CDN thumbnail while asset_license_and_download_stock returned a genuine 7360x4912 file, which is exactly the gap the third checkpoint sits in. crop_and_resize's silent interpolation to a 2x cap, reported only inside its tradeoffs, is what makes the thumbnail arithmetic a real gate rather than an assertion. VECTOR: the disjoint wordmark collapse under remove_background (1,743 opaque px out of roughly 18,000 of ink), the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero are live findings, and the acceptance bar scores the hygiene the tool does not perform. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, and transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end, including a browser proving licensed faces load, with the case sensitivity and non standard numeric weight traps live. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed (it always returns zero hits), license verified with a real full resolution download, boards persist with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. VIDEO AND AUDIO: metadata, summarise, quick cut (shorten only), resize (downscale only) and enhance speech are submitted through the connector's asynchronous media path and resolve on the host's progress surface; no checkpoint and no automatic verifier in this task depends on byte inspecting a video file, and every gradeable motion criterion is either a dimension read off the delivered file or something a reviewer watches. AVOIDED: no video trim to timestamp, no format conversion, no frame rate conversion, no upscaling, no vector render or vector merge, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no text to image, no compositing, no OCR, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20.
